The League Rejected and the Red Scare

🔊 Read aloud: listen to this page
THIS WEEK

This week follows the United States from the Armistice to 1922. You will see why the Senate rejected the League of Nations, how fear of revolution shaped 1919 and 1920, and why the country narrowed its door to immigrants.

Take the pages in this order: the lesson "The League Rejected, 1919 to 1922," then the source Henry Cabot Lodge, Speech Against the League of Nations, then the lesson "Red Scare, Strikes, and the Closing Door," and then the source A. Mitchell Palmer, "The Case Against the 'Reds'". Read each lesson before the source that follows it, since the lessons give you the background you need to read the sources well.

What to turn in: this week's main assignment is a Primary Source Report. You will also take part in the discussion "Who Killed the League: Wilson or the Senate?" Instructions, due dates, and links for both are in Canvas.

When you finish, open the Week Wrap-Up page and use its checklist to confirm that everything is submitted.
